samples.summary: moveVertical() still calls findVisualLine() without affinity, so it resolves a wrap boundary to the *later* line while the rest of the editor now resolves it to the caret's line
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4165 `const info = findVisualLine(lb, pos);` — the only other caller of the changed helper, left on the new `'forward'` default. Meanwhile getPixelForPosition() two lines earlier (4104) already hit-tests with `this.cursor.lineAffinity`, so the two halves of moveVertical disagree at a boundary. This inconsistency is newly reachable from the keyboard: after this change `handleEnd` (2799 + `cursor.moveTo(newPos)` at 2806, which defaults affinity to 'backward' per cursor.ts:28) reliably parks the caret exactly on a character-wrap boundary with 'backward' affinity — the very state the new test at packages/docs/test/view/visual-line-affinity.test.ts:151 creates. In that state findVisualLine returns lineIndex i+1, so the `isFirstLine` special case at 4168/4170 (jump to line start on ArrowUp from the first visual line) and the symmetric `isLastLine` case at 4174 no longer fire, and ArrowUp/ArrowDown at the boundary can appear to do nothing. The project's own todo (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-visual-line-affinity-todo.md:59) declares this a non-goal, which is why I flag it at medium confidence — but the non-goal reasoning ('its findVisualLine use is only a first/last-line check') is exactly the check that breaks. Fix belongs at text-editor.ts:4165 (pass `this.cursor.lineAffinity`).

samples.summary: getVisualLineRange/Start/End now silently read mutable cursor state for an arbitrary `pos` argument, an undocumented coupling for any future caller passing a non-cursor position
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4001, 4053, 4061 default the new parameter to `this.cursor.lineAffinity`. The helpers take an arbitrary `pos: DocPosition` but now resolve it using the *cursor's* affinity. All three current callers (2786, 2799, 2845) do pass `this.cursor.position`, so nothing is broken today, and the JSDoc at 3997 notes the assumption — but the result of these helpers is no longer a pure function of `pos`, so a caller resolving a selection anchor or a remote/peer position (e.g. anything analogous to peer-cursor.ts:99, which threads its own affinity explicitly) would get the local caret's affinity applied to someone else's offset.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. findVisualLine() gained a third lineAffinity param defaulting to 'forward' (visual-line.ts:21-24), whose boundary rule (visual-line.ts:38-39) resolves a non-last wrap boundary to line i+1. moveVertical() calls it with no affinity at text-editor.ts:4165 while the same function hit-tests pixels with this.cursor.lineAffinity at :4104 and :4119, so the two halves disagree at a boundary. The disagreement suppresses the isFirstLine/isLastLine special cases at :4168-4177, letting moveVertical fall through to returning the unchanged result at :4204-4205 (ArrowUp/ArrowDown appear inert). The required state — caret parked exactly on a character-wrap boundary with 'backward' affinity — is reachable from the keyboard: handleEnd (:2799 getVisualLineEnd, :2806 cursor.moveTo(newPos)) plus the 'backward' default in cursor.ts:28, the same state the new tests build at test/view/visual-line-affinity.test.ts:136-158. The todo's non-goal note (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-visual-line-affinity-todo.md:57-61) is a scope declaration in a doc, not a guard, and its rationale rests on the very first/last-line check that breaks; a repo doc cannot refute a reachable inconsistency. This is a consumer of a changed helper left on the old contract — in-lane for blast-radius at major.
